title: Overview
text: pharmaverse rapidly emerged open-source standard clinical trial reporting. Core packages sdtm.oak support SDTM transformations, admiral provides robust framework ADaM derivations. Downstream, rich ecosystem visualization tools enables production-ready outputs — including tabular summaries gtsummary safety visualizations via safetyCharts. time, CDISC Analysis Results Standard (ARS) gaining momentum, packages like cards beginning support ARS-aligned workflows. Complementing traditional static deliverables, many organizations increasingly adopting Shiny web-based review tools enable interactive exploration clinical data. parallel, gsm framework — particularly gsm.core package — matured YAML-driven workflow engine designed deliver reproducible, traceable, audit-ready pipelines clinical data science. framework currently powers standardized Risk-Based Quality Monitoring (RBQM) infrastructure, pairing flexible data workflows robust reporting systems demonstrated gsm.kri. Historically, pharmaverse gsm ecosystems evolved along separate trajectories. However, complementary strengths present compelling opportunity integration: combining pharmaverse’s domain-specific data standards reporting capabilities gsm’s workflow orchestration auditability form foundation fully traceable, end--end clinical reporting pipeline.

title: Overview
text: gsm engine: framework, workflows defined declaratively using YAML configuration files organized three sections: Meta — captures descriptive metadata documentation associated workflow Spec — declares required data sources structural requirements, defining inputs needed downstream derivations transformations Steps — specifies execution pipeline. step written {output, name, params} block: , output represents returned object, name identifies function executed, params contains function arguments. runtime, RunWorkflows() parses step definitions orchestrates execution sequentially, effectively reproducing behavior piped R command. Raw → SDTM (gsm + sdtm.oak): Raw eCRF data transformed SDTM using gsm-driven workflows aligned established sdtm.oak implementation patterns. workflow mirrors VS domain example official vignette, demonstrating standardized SDTM mappings can embedded within reproducible YAML pipeline. reference implementation available . SDTM → ADaM (gsm + admiral): SDTM domains reintroduced workflow engine processed admiral derivations construct ADaM datasets. Functions derive_vars_merged() derive_param_map() generated ADVS parameters analysis values (e.g., MAP), derivation logic expressed via !expr tags. approach preserves transparency ensuring transformations remain reproducible audit-ready. admiral vignette demonstrates functions can found . ADaM → TFLs (gsm + gtsummary + safetyCharts): resulting ADaM datasets fed directly visualization steps, invoking gtsummary tabular summaries safetyCharts graphical outputs. enables generation publication-ready TFLs within fully traceable end--end pipeline, adaptable organization’s visualization standards. Beyond static reporting, workflows can automatically refresh web-based HTML applications new data derived, supporting near real-time exploratory analysis safety review. ADaM → ARS (gsm + cards): parallel, derived ADaM datasets extended using cards prototype ARS-aligned datasets outputs. Although ARS standard still evolving, example illustrates emerging libraries can integrated gsm framework minimal friction, enabling early adoption new reporting standards within existing, reproducible workflow.

code: ## ```yaml ## meta: ##   ID: ADVS ##   Type: ADAM ##   Description: Create Basic ADSL ##   Priority: 1 ## spec: ##   SDTM_DM: ##     _all: ##       required: true ##   SDTM_VS: ##     _all: ##       required: true ## steps: ##   - output: initial_advs ##     name: admiral::derive_vars_merged ##     params: ##       dataset: SDTM_VS ##       dataset_add: SDTM_DM ##       new_vars: !expr exprs(TRT01A) ##       by_vars: !expr exprs(STUDYID, USUBJID) ##   - output: advs ##     name: dplyr::mutate ##     params: ##       .data: initial_advs ##       PARAMCD: !expr rlang::expr(.data[["VSTESTCD"]]) ##       AVAL: !expr rlang::expr(.data[["VSORRES"]]) ##   - output: advs ##     name: admiral::derive_param_map ##     params: ##       dataset: advs ##       by_vars: !expr exprs(STUDYID, USUBJID, TRT01A, VSDTC, VISIT, VISITNUM, VSTPT, VSTPTNUM) ##       sysbp_code: 'SYSBP' ##       diabp_code: 'DIABP' ##       get_unit_expr: !expr rlang::expr(.data[["VSORRESU"]]) ## ``` ADAM_workflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(   strNames = "ADVS",   strPath = "demo_gsmpharmaverse/workflows/2_SDTM_TO_ADAM/",   strPackage = "workr" ) ADAM <- workr::RunWorkflows(lWorkflows = ADAM_workflows, lData = sdtm) map2(ADAM, names(ADAM), function(x,y) arrow::write_parquet(x, paste0("demo_gsmpharmaverse/data/ADAM/",y,".parquet"))

title: Workflow Execution Helpers
text: {workr} provides minimal mental model describing executing data workflows: Workflows YAML files meta (workflow metadata) steps (ordered list function calls) Steps functions accept data parameters, producing output gets added shared data list Meta workflow-level configuration accessible steps package provides three core functions: RunStep() - execute single workflow step RunWorkflow() - execute workflow specification (YAML) RunWorkflows() - run multiple workflows sequence

title: Workflow Execution Helpers
text: {workr} built solve specific problem: reusable, customizable data pipelines complex clinical trial monitoring. core functions {workr} originally implemented part {gsm} framework risk-based quality montoring (RBQM). {gsm} team developed stable, reusable model generating metrics monitor clinical trials. challenge figuring run metrics across large portfolio; Take 30 studies monthly snapshots, needing 15 metrics computed 5 steps get 27,000 metric computations per year. make things complex, study slightly different requirements, maintaining individual scripts quickly becomes unmaintainable. {workr}’s solution: Define workflows , customize via meta parameters, compose larger pipelines.

title: Workflow Execution Helpers
text: Define workflow YAML: Run R:
code: # hello_cars.yaml meta:   ID: hello_cars   col: speed steps:   - name: dplyr::pull      output: speed     params:       df: df       col: col   - name: mean     output: result     params:       lData: speed wf <- yaml::read_yaml("hello_cars.yaml") lData <- list(df = cars)  result <- workr::RunWorkflow(   lWorkflow = wf,   lData = lData )  result <- workr::RunWorkflow(   lWorkflow = wf,   lData = lData )  # result = 15.4 (mean of cars$speed)

title: Workflow Execution Helpers
text: step workflow: 1. Calls function (specified step$name) 2. Passes parameters params (resolving references lData, meta, literal values) 3. Saves result lData using output name 4. Makes available next step chaining steps together, build complex pipelines simple, reusable components.

title: Workflow Execution Helpers
text: Workflows can call workflows! Use RunWorkflow step name nest workflows:
code: meta:   ID: parent steps:   - name: RunWorkflow     output: child_result     params:       lWorkflow: child_workflow       lData: lData   - name: process_result     output: final     params:       data: child_result

title: Workflow Execution Helpers
text: Example workflow YAML files provided inst/workflows/: - helloworld.yaml - simple single-step workflow - two_steps.yaml - multi-step workflow - cars.yaml - regression example Load run example:
code: wf <- yaml::read_yaml(   system.file("workflows", "cars.yaml", package = "workr") ) lData <- list(cars = cars) model <- workr::RunWorkflow(wf, lData) summary(model)

text: MakeWorkflowList() utility function creates list workflows use KRI pipelines.

title: Load workflows from a package/directory. — MakeWorkflowList
code: MakeWorkflowList(   strNames = NULL,   strPath = "workflow",   strPackage = NULL,   bExact = FALSE,   bRecursive = TRUE )

title: Load workflows from a package/directory. — MakeWorkflowList
text: strNames array character List workflows include. NULL (default) includes workflows specified locations. strPath character location workflow YAML files. NULL (default), function look /inst/workflow folder. strPackage character package name workflow YAML files located. NULL, package use absolute path. bExact logical strName matches exact? false, partial matches included. Default FALSE. bRecursive logical Find files nested folders? Default TRUE

title: Load workflows from a package/directory. — MakeWorkflowList
text: list list workflows workflow parameter metadata.

title: Run a SQL query on a data frame or DuckDB table — RunQuery
text: Executes SQL query data frame DuckDB lazy table, creating -memory DuckDB table needed. query must include df placeholder.

title: Run a SQL query on a data frame or DuckDB table — RunQuery
code: RunQuery(strQuery, df, bUseSchema = FALSE, lColumnMapping = NULL)

title: Run a SQL query on a data frame or DuckDB table — RunQuery
text: strQuery character SQL query run, containing "df". df data.frame tbl_dbi SQL query. bUseSchema boolean enforce data types schema. lColumnMapping list column specifications bUseSchema = TRUE.

title: Run a SQL query on a data frame or DuckDB table — RunQuery
text: data.frame query results.

title: Run a SQL query on a data frame or DuckDB table — RunQuery
code: if (requireNamespace("DBI", quietly = TRUE) &&     requireNamespace("dbplyr", quietly = TRUE) &&     requireNamespace("duckdb", quietly = TRUE)) {   df <- data.frame(     Name = c("John", "Jane", "Bob"),     Age = c(25, 30, 35),     Salary = c(50000, 60000, 70000)   )    query <- "SELECT Name, Salary FROM df WHERE Age >= 30"   RunQuery(query, df) } #> [INFO] Creating a new temporary DuckDB connection. #> [INFO] SQL Query complete: 2 rows returned. #> [INFO] Disconnected from temporary DuckDB connection. #>   Name Salary #> 1 Jane  60000 #> 2  Bob  70000

title: Run a single step in a workflow — RunStep
code: RunStep(lStep, lData, lMeta, lSpec = NULL)

title: Run a single step in a workflow — RunStep
text: lStep list single workflow step. lData list named list domain level data frames. lMeta list named list meta data. lSpec list data specification containing required columns.

title: Run a single step in a workflow — RunStep
text: Results function call specified lStep$name.

title: Run a single step in a workflow — RunStep
code: sum_step <- function(lData, y) lData$value + y lStep <- list(name = "sum_step", output = "result", params = list(lData = "lData", y = "value")) lData <- list(value = 2) RunStep(lStep = lStep, lData = lData, lMeta = list()) #> [INFO] Evaluating 2 parameter(s) for `sum_step` #> [INFO] lData = lData:  Passing full lData object. #> [INFO] y = value: Passing lData$value. #> [INFO] Calling `sum_step` #> Error in GetStrFunctionIfNamespaced(lStep$name): Function 'sum_step' not found.
